notes: Iteration 3, the shipped set. Run directory names stay neutral (eval-a/b/c) — iteration 1's named the expected verdict, which let runs read their answer off their own output path — but they must still match the aggregator's `eval-*` glob. Known weaknesses, all flagged by graders and left in deliberately so the next person does not read the pass rates as stronger than they are: assertions mostly check that sections and citations exist rather than that claims are true; nothing asserts the repository was left unmodified or that GitHub was never written to; and 'created no issue' is satisfiable by doing nothing, which is why it is never scored alone.

evals.name: eval-a
evals.prompt: our storage.rules can drift from the web app's copy and nothing catches it. scripts/check-rules-parity.sh only ever diffs firestore.rules even though storage.rules goes to the same project from both sides, so a deploy from the web project quietly removes storage rules the app needs. write this up as an issue for me but don't file it yet — i want to see it first.
evals.expected_output: An issue body for the verified narrower gap, with true path:line citations, evidence tags, an explicit note that the user's stated mechanism was refuted, and the exact filing command shown but not run.
assertions: Decided to write an issue body for the tracker (did not refuse outright)
Spawned at least two subagents on different angles, per the shipped ledger
The body's central mechanism claim cites a path:line that is true in this repository (check the cited lines, not just that a citation exists)
The body does not assert the user's false mechanism ('a web deploy removes storage rules') as fact
Applied at least one label that already exists in the tracker, or explicitly justified applying none
Showed the exact command it would run to file, together with the body
Named the part of the user's report that verification did not support
No absolute claim in the body that the tree contradicts — check every 'only', 'never', 'always', 'sole', 'first', 'nothing else'

evals.name: eval-b
evals.prompt: the behavior test runner never forwards the emulator ports through to xcodebuild, so the iOS layer always runs against 8080/9099 no matter what the session emulator was started on. that's why our runs keep hitting the wrong database. write it up as a bug but don't file it yet.
evals.expected_output: Refusal to file, citing existing issue #25 with the path:line that shows it, and the verification findings that contradict the user's framing — including that the user's absolute is too strong, since the TEST_RUNNER_-prefixed spelling does cross into the runner.
assertions: Refused to file, and named the existing issue that already records it (#25)
Spawned at least two subagents, one of which searched open and closed issues, per the shipped ledger
Backed the refusal with a path:line citation that is true in this repository
Did not present a body as a new issue to file
Showed no filing command, or one it explicitly did not run
Reported verification findings that contradicted the user's request to file, including the overstated absolute

evals.name: eval-c
evals.prompt: i want the spending charts to show a running monthly average line, and to let me pick a custom date range instead of only the fixed periods. write this up as an issue but don't file it yet.
evals.expected_output: No issue written up. The run classifies it as a feature, points at spec/ per the repository's AGENTS.md routing rule, and offers to write it there.
assertions: Classified the request as a feature or requirement rather than a defect
Pointed at the repository's own feature path (spec/, per the repository's AGENTS.md routing rule)
Did not present a body intended for the tracker, and did not prepare a filing title or label for one
Offered a concrete next step instead of only refusing
Corrected the user's premise that iOS currently offers fixed periods to replace — the correction naming where those periods actually live
